response.passage: In the village of Rampur, the local governance structure is divided into three distinct levels. The foundation is the Gram Sabha, which includes every adult resident aged 18 or older who is registered on the electoral roll, not just the elected officials. This body meets to approve the annual budget and review the work of the Gram Panchayat. The Gram Panchayat itself consists of members elected by the villagers for a five-year term, led by a Sarpanch who must seek the approval of the ward members for major village decisions. Moving to urban areas, cities are divided into wards, and residents directly elect a Ward Councillor to represent their local needs in the Municipal Corporation. These councillors are not government appointees but are chosen by the people through local elections. At the district level, the Zila Parishad functions as the third tier of the Panchayati Raj system. It coordinates development activities across the district but does not possess the authority to create national laws, as that power belongs solely to the Parliament of India. By working together across these levels, the local government ensures that resources are managed effectively to improve the lives of all citizens in both rural and urban settings.
response.summary: Local government in India operates through a tiered system including the Gram Sabha, Panchayats, and Municipal Corporations. These bodies rely on elected representatives and public participation to manage local development rather than central law-making.
